exposure: Severe perineal lacerations (SPLs) during first delivery
cohort: 947,035 women in Sweden who had a singleton live birth between 1992 and 2013
finding: Experiencing severe perineal laceration during a first delivery was associated with slightly fewer overall births, but no difference in the probability of a second birth or interpregnancy interval, and an increased likelihood of scheduled cesarean in subsequent births.
mod_finding: Women who experience severe perineal lacerations (SPL) during their first delivery are more likely to have a scheduled cesarean birth for subsequent pregnancies.
